claims.object_text: mouse model with cell-type specific Depdc5 deletion (excitatory or inhibitory neurons)
claims.quote: Depdc5 was specifically deleted in excitatory or inhibitory neurons in the mouse brain to determine neuronal subtypes that drive epileptogenesis and SUDEP.

claims.object_text: Depdc5 deletion in excitatory neurons (cortical layer 5 and dentate gyrus) causes frequent generalized tonic-clonic seizures and SUDEP in young adult mice
claims.quote: Depdc5 deletion in excitatory neurons in cortical layer 5 and dentate gyrus caused frequent generalized tonic-clonic seizures and SUDEP in young adult mice, but Depdc5 deletion in cortical interneurons did not.

claims.object_text: Depdc5 deletion in cortical interneurons does not cause the same seizures/SUDEP phenotype
claims.quote: but Depdc5 deletion in cortical interneurons did not.

claims.object_text: EEG suppression immediately following ictal offset observed in seizures
claims.quote: EEG suppression immediately following ictal offset was observed in fatal and non-fatal seizures,

claims.object_text: loss of low amplitude rhythmic theta frequency activity occurs only in fatal seizures
claims.quote: low amplitude rhythmic theta frequency activity was lost only in fatal seizures.

claims.object_text: baseline respiratory dysfunction prior to SUDEP in Depdc5-deficient mice
claims.quote: these mice developed baseline respiratory dysfunction prior to SUDEP,

claims.object_text: ictal apnea occurs long before terminal cardiac asystole
claims.quote: ictal apnea occurred long before terminal cardiac asystole.

claims.object_text: Ictal apnea and respiratory dysregulation contribute causally to SUDEP pathophysiology
claims.quote: Ictal apnea and respiratory dysregulation play critical roles in SUDEP.
